newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING Q1 loan value adjustments Dfl 200 mln.
newsitem.headline: ING Q1 loan value adjustments Dfl 200 mln.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Thursday that value adjustments to the receivables of its banking operations in the first quarter of 1997 totalled 200 million guilders.
Announcing its first quarter results, the group said it also added 45 million guilders to the new fund for general banking risks (FAR).
In the first three months of 1996, ING's value adjustments to receivables amounted to 275 million guilders.
The FAR did not exist until this year.
From the start of this year ING, along with other Dutch banks, introduced the FAR fund to replace the fund for general contingencies (VAR), which contained its hidden reserves.
The reserves, built up as ING overprovided for loan losses, had to be revealed ahead of changes to European banking laws.
It transferred 1.30 billion guilders from the VAR to the new FAR fund, which is for unexpected loan losses, and added the remaining 1.25 billion from the VAR to shareholders equity.
ING is now deducting actual loan losses directly from its profit and loss account, whereas previously they were covered by additions to the VAR fund.
ING said it added 45 million guilders to the FAR in the first quarter of 1997 because of the continued rise of risk-weighted assets.
It said the net amount in the FAR fund stood at 1.34 billion guilders, after tax and exchange rate differences.
